title: capsicum annuum subsp. baccatum
intro: Capsicum annuum subsp. baccatum, commonly known as the Bolivian pepper or Aji amarillo, is a subspecies of the Capsicum annuum plant, a species of flowering plant in the nightshade family. The Bolivian pepper is a perennial plant native to the Andean region, and its fruits have been used in traditional medicine for their numerous health benefits. The plant is rich in antioxidants, anti-inflammatory compounds, and other bioactive constituents, which have been shown to exhibit therapeutic actions such as analgesic, anti-diabetic, and antimicrobial effects, contributing to its traditional use in treating various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of the Bolivian pepper include capsaicinoids, flavonoids, carotenoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its potential health benefits, including reducing inflammation, improving cardiovascular health, and boosting the immune system.
